title: Hosted API endpoint contracts, compatibility shim, and rollout runbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: This PRD defines the API contracts, backwards-compatibility shim, operational rollout plan, and acceptance criteria for publishing the unified hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) in the hosted API. The goal is to deliver a single stable surface that: 1) preserves current customer integrations, 2) enables new structured output and tool-calling features, and 3) provides clear rollback and throttling behavior. This doc focuses on contract-level compatibility, metrics/telemetry gating, staged traffic ramping, and the checklist runbook for launch and rollback. It intentionally separates implementation details (runtime kernel selection, quantization) into ENG tickets and surfaces only the behavioral and integration constraints required for product teams and customers.
goals: Provide a stable API contract for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank that is backwards compatible with existing hosted endpoints
Define a compatibility shim to accept legacy payload shapes and map them to the unified surface
Ship observability gates and SLO checks that must pass before each rollout step
Create a clear rollout runbook with traffic tiers, monitoring dashboards, and rollback criteria
non_goals: Rewriting or deprecating customer prompts or stored prompts
Any change that requires customer-side SDK changes beyond an opt-in flag
Model architecture changes — those are handled in model onboarding tickets
user_stories: As a product engineer, I can call the unified completions/chat endpoint without changing my existing HTTP payloads so my integration does not break
As an ML engineer, I can request structured outputs and function-calling while traffic is still routed to older model variants
As a platform engineer, I can gradually increase traffic and automatically stop the rollout when key regressions appear in eval metrics
api_contract_summary: The unified surface will expose distinct route paths (/v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank). Each route accepts both the legacy and new payload schemas via a compatibility shim. Backwards-compatible mapping rules are in the mapping table linked below. New fields (structured_output, function_call) are opt-in and default to legacy behavior for existing fields. Error responses retain current status codes with an additional machine-readable 'compat_version' header when a shim translation occurred.
compatibility_shim_details: Shim accepts legacy fields: prompt -> messages[0], temperature as float or string
Auto-populate missing required new-fields with safe defaults (e.g., structured_output=false)
Record 'compat_translation' boolean in request trace for debugging
Reject payloads that explicitly request a removed legacy mode with 400 and clear error message
acceptance_criteria: All four routes return successful responses for a suite of 500+ legacy integration tests (fixtures provided)
Compatibility shim introduces no more than 1ms p50 added latency on average in synthetic tests
Telemetry emits compat_translation, compat_version, and shim_latency metrics to Console within the initial rollout window
Canary traffic stage (1% global) shows no regression in latency P95, error rate, or model-quality evals for 48h
Automated rollback triggers if latency P95 increases by >25% or error rate increases by >0.5% absolute over baseline
Docs and SDK changelog published and linked in API dashboard before 1% canary completes
Security review completed and sign-off recorded (security_review_required=true)
telemetry_and_slos: Emit per-route token-level latency, request counts, and error codes
Model-quality evals: run sample prompt set every 6h and compare to baseline embeddings similarity and response scoring
SLOs: 99th percentile latency under 600ms for chat baseline, 99.9% availability
Alerting: immediate PagerDuty when canary eval fails or error rate trigger fires
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dry run using staging keys (internal teams and alpha partners). Stage 1: 1% global canary for 72h with extended telemetry retention. Stage 2: 10% traffic for 48h with expanded customer subset. Stage 3: 50% for 24h. Stage 4: full rollout and deprecation mode for legacy bindings after 90 days. At each stage, a designated owner must mark the stage passed in the runbook checklist and confirm no blocking alerts. The rollout automation will allow emergency immediate rollback to the previous variant.
rollback_criteria: Latency P95 increased >25% vs baseline during stage
Error rate rise >0.5% absolute and sustained for 15 minutes
Model-quality eval score drop >3% on critical prompt set
Any customer-reported data loss or corruption
Security incident or missing audit logs
launch_checklist: SDK change log and opt-in flags documented
Telemetry and dashboards created in Console (links below)
Runbook owner assigned and on-call rota updated
Customer communication drafts ready (blog, changelog, emails)
Legal/compliance sign-off for data residency and KMS usage
Support playbook and troubleshooting runbook published
Post-launch eval plan and rollback criteria confirmed

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shim complexity leads to subtle semantic differences. Mitigation: exhaustive fixture test suite and translation trace in logs
Risk: Increased latency. Mitigation: performance budget for shim (target <2ms median), and fallback to bypass shim for high-QPS customers if required
Risk: Customer confusion about new fields. Mitigation: opt-in flags, in-console migration guides, and SDK helpers
